h1: The 6 Best Privacy-Focused Robot Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 camera-free robot vacuums from roborock and eufy, scored on navigation without a lens, dock automation and everyday value.
summary: The roborock Q7 M5+ is the privacy-minded pick we would buy: LiDAR navigation instead of a camera, 10,000Pa suction and a self-empty base listed at 7 to 9 weeks per emptying. The roborock Q10 S5+ is the cheaper step with the same camera-free approach. The eufy Omni C20 and C28 are the premium docks, and the eufy 11S MAX is the simplest hardware here, with no mop and no camera.
intro: A robot vacuum roams every room of your home, so it is fair to ask what it can see. The biggest privacy line in this category is simple: some models carry a camera for object recognition, and some navigate with a spinning laser sensor that only measures distance. A laser sensor cannot capture a picture of your living room.

We reviewed six robots whose listings point to navigation without an onboard camera, and ranked them on that approach plus dock automation, mopping and price. One caution applies to all of them: an app and a Wi-Fi connection still exist on most, so camera-free is not the same as offline. Rankings come from spec sheets and owner reports.

products.name: roborock Q7 M5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop, Up to 7-9 Weeks Self-Empty, 10000Pa
products.verdict: LiDAR navigation with no camera, 10,000Pa and a long self-empty interval.
products.description:
The Q7 M5+ is a vacuum and mop combo that navigates with LiDAR and no camera, with 10,000Pa suction and a self-empty base listed at 7 to 9 weeks per emptying. Fewer sensors pointed at your rooms means less to worry about.

It ranks first because it matches the Q10 S5+ on suction and adds the longest interval, so you touch it less. Against the eufy models, it costs far less than the C28 and Omni C20.

Best for a household that wants a camera-free robot with minimal chores. Caveat: it still uses an app, so read the privacy settings.

products.name: roborock Q10 S5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop, 10,000Pa Suction
products.verdict: The same camera-free LiDAR approach with a self-empty base, for under $300.
products.description:
The Q10 S5+ uses LiDAR with no camera, 10,000Pa suction, a self-empty base and a mop. It sits between the Q7 L5 and the Q7 M5+ in the range.

It ranks second because the Q7 M5+ lists a longer empty interval for a small step up. It beats the Q7 L5 by adding a dock and 2,000 more Pa.

Best for a mid-budget buyer who wants a camera-free robot with a dock. Caveat: no interval is listed.
products.skipIf: You want the longest empty window.

products.name: eufy Omni C20 Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo for Hardwood and Carpet
products.verdict: LiDAR without a camera, a self-empty base and hardwood and carpet capability.
products.description:
Mapping on the Omni C20 comes from LiDAR alone, which leaves no camera on the robot itself. It is a vacuum and mop combo with a self-empty base, capable on hardwood and carpet.

It ranks third because the roborock models cost less for similar camera-free navigation. It is the cheaper eufy, with a dock that does more than the Q7 L5.

Best for buyers who prefer the eufy brand. Caveat: the listing gives no suction number.
products.idealFor: Buyers who prefer the eufy brand.

products.name: eufy C28 Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo, 15,000 Pa, HydroJet Roller Mop
products.verdict: The highest suction here, 15,000 Pa, with a roller mop and no camera.
products.description:
The C28 is the most powerful and expensive model in this guide, with 15,000 Pa of suction and a HydroJet roller mop. It relies on LiDAR for navigation, keeping a camera off the robot, and has a self-empty base.

It ranks fourth only because of price: the roborock Q7 M5+ offers the same privacy approach for much less. For pet hair and embedded debris, the extra suction is the point.

Best for a large home with pets that wants camera-free navigation. Caveat: the cost is high.
products.idealFor: Large pet homes wanting camera-free cleaning.

products.name: roborock Q7 L5 Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo, 8,000Pa Suction
products.verdict: LiDAR mapping and a mop for under $150.
products.description:
The Q7 L5 brings roborock's LiDAR mapping and combo vacuum and mop function to under $150. It lists 8,000Pa suction and app-based mapping, with no camera.

It ranks fifth because it has no self-empty dock, which the models above all include. That is the price of the low cost.

Best for a small home on a strict budget. Caveat: you will empty the bin yourself.
products.idealFor: Small homes on a strict budget.

products.name: eufy 11S MAX Robot Vacuum Cleaner, Super Thin, Quiet
products.verdict: A thin, quiet, vacuum-only robot with no camera and no mop tank.
products.description:
The 11S MAX is a thin, quiet, vacuum-only robot with no mop tank and no camera. Fewer onboard features means fewer things to worry about from a privacy point of view.

It ranks last because it is the plainest machine here, with no dock and no mop. In exchange, it is simple, inexpensive and well known.

Best for a small home that wants the least connected hardware. Caveat: basic navigation and manual emptying.
products.idealFor: Small homes wanting minimal connected hardware.
products.skipIf: You want mapping or a dock.

whatMatters.detail: LiDAR is a spinning laser that measures distance and builds a floor plan. It cannot capture a picture. Camera robots use a lens to recognize objects and can in principle capture images. If you want the strongest privacy, look for LiDAR in the specs and check for the words no camera.

Even a camera-free robot connects to an app that stores your floor plan and schedule. Read the maker's privacy page, turn off any optional sharing and use a strong account password. If you want no cloud link, choose a model that can run from buttons alone.
Without a camera, a robot cannot tell a sock from a cable. It will bump into them. Pick up floor clutter before each run, and be ready to rescue it from the occasional cord.
Put the robot on a guest network if your router has one. That keeps it away from your computers. Check the router's settings page for a guest option.
A self-empty base cuts how often you carry the bin around. That is a convenience, not a privacy feature, but it makes a camera-free robot practical for a busy household.

faq.q: Does a robot vacuum without a camera still use Wi-Fi?
faq.a: Usually yes, for the app. LiDAR models like the roborock Q10 S5+ have no lens but still connect to a cloud service.
It only measures distance, so it cannot capture an image. It does store a floor plan in the app.

faq.q: Is the roborock Q7 M5+ worth more than the Q7 L5?
faq.a: If you want a dock and a long interval, yes. For a small home with a tight budget, the Q7 L5 is fine.

faq.q: Will a camera-free robot avoid cables?
faq.a: Not reliably. Without a camera it cannot identify cords, so pick them up first.

faq.q: Can I use a robot vacuum on a guest network?
faq.a: Usually yes. Put it on the guest Wi-Fi if your router offers one.

faq.q: Which is simplest in terms of connected features?
faq.a: The eufy 11S MAX, a plain vacuum with no mop and no camera.

finalTake: If you want a robot vacuum that keeps a lens out of your home, the roborock Q7 M5+ is the best buy: LiDAR navigation, 10,000Pa suction and the longest self-empty window. The Q10 S5+ is the mid-range alternative, and the eufy C28 is the premium choice for pet homes. On a budget, the Q7 L5 keeps LiDAR for under $150, and the eufy 11S MAX is the simplest hardware here.
